Prepare and Export Survey Sample Points for CAPI Fieldwork Apps

Source: R/vantor_fieldwork.R
vantor_export_capi.Rd

Enriches a set of survey sample locations (sf points or polygons, such as household structures, enumeration clusters, or ground-truth plots) with navigation and preload fields ready for ODK Collect, KoboToolbox, ArcGIS Survey123, World Bank Survey Solutions, and QField:

  • sample_id: Unique formatted sample identifier

  • longitude, latitude: WGS84 decimal degree coordinates

  • odk_geopoint: Preload string ("<lat> <lon> 0 0") used by ODK / Kobo geopoint questions

  • plus_code: Offline-capable 10-character Google Plus Code via vantor_plus_code()

  • google_maps_url: One-click navigation link for mobile enumerators

  • Optional grid cell assignment (cell_id) if a grid from vantor_survey_grid() is supplied

  • Optional imagery vintage metadata (acq_date, sensor, gsd_m) if seamlines are supplied

Usage

vantor_export_capi(
  samples,
  id_col = NULL,
  grid = NULL,
  seamlines = NULL,
  output_csv = NULL,
  output_geojson = NULL,
  output_suso_tab = NULL,
  suso_gps_var = NULL,
  verbose = getOption("vantorr.verbose", TRUE)
)

Arguments

samples

An sf object (POINT or POLYGON; polygons are converted to representative points via sf::st_point_on_surface()).

id_col

Character string. Optional existing column name in samples to use as sample_id. If NULL, generates sequential IDs ("S001", "S002", ...).

grid

Optional sf grid from vantor_survey_grid() used to assign each sample to its Enumeration Area / grid cell_id.

seamlines

Optional sf seamline polygons from vantor_get_seamlines() used to attach imagery vintage (imagery_acq_date, imagery_sensor) to each sample point.

output_csv

Optional file path to write a CSV preload table (for ODK Collect, KoboToolbox, and ArcGIS Survey123). Default is NULL.

output_geojson

Optional file path to write a GeoJSON file for mobile GIS map overlays (QField, Mergin Maps). Default is NULL.

output_suso_tab

Optional file path to write a tab-delimited (.tab) assignment preload file formatted for World Bank Survey Solutions Headquarters (Upload Assignments). Includes composite GPS columns (<suso_gps_var>__Latitude and <suso_gps_var>__Longitude) so sampled structures appear as interactive pins on the Interviewer tablet Map Dashboard over the .tpk basemap, plus _target_area (from cell_id), plus_code, and imagery_acq_date. Default is NULL.

suso_gps_var

Optional character string. Variable name of the identifying GPS question in Survey Solutions Designer (e.g., "hh_gps"). When provided (or when output_suso_tab is set), the coordinate columns on both the returned sf object and the exported .tab file are named <suso_gps_var>__Latitude and <suso_gps_var>__Longitude instead of latitude and longitude. Default is NULL (uses "hh_gps" automatically when output_suso_tab is supplied).

verbose

Logical. Print progress messages. Default is getOption("vantorr.verbose", TRUE).

Value

An enriched sf point object in EPSG:4326.

Details

Optionally writes the enriched dataset to a CSV preload table (output_csv) and/or a GeoJSON file (output_geojson).

Examples

pts <- sf::st_as_sf(
  data.frame(
    hh_id = c("HH_01", "HH_02"),
    lon = c(-105.005, -105.002),
    lat = c(39.735, 39.738)
  ),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = 4326
)

capi_sf <- vantor_export_capi(pts, id_col = "hh_id", suso_gps_var = "hh_gps", verbose = FALSE)
head(capi_sf)
#> Simple feature collection with 2 features and 7 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -105.005 ymin: 39.735 xmax: -105.002 ymax: 39.738
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>   hh_id                geometry sample_id hh_gps__Latitude hh_gps__Longitude
#> 1 HH_01 POINT (-105.005 39.735)     HH_01           39.735          -105.005
#> 2 HH_02 POINT (-105.002 39.738)     HH_02           39.738          -105.002
#>                odk_geopoint   plus_code
#> 1 39.735000 -105.005000 0 0 85FPPXPW+22
#> 2 39.738000 -105.002000 0 0 85FPPXQX+66
#>                                                         google_maps_url
#> 1 https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=39.735000,-105.005000
#> 2 https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=39.738000,-105.002000
